newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ATLANTA ATHLETIC CLUB TO HOST 2001 PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ATLANTA ATHLETIC CLUB TO HOST 2001 PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Atlanta Athletic Club, which the legendary Bobby Jones considered his home club, will host the PGA Championship in 2001, the PGA of America announced on Wednesday.

The club, which will mark its 100th anniversay next year, will be hosting its third major championship -- after the 1976 U.S. Open, which was won by Jerry Pate, and the 1981 PGA, which was won by local resident Larry Nelson.

Jones, often considered the greatest golfer ever, always listed Atlanta Athletic Club as his home course, even though he founded Augusta National Golf Club, home of the Masters, and is that club's president in perpetuity.
The selection of Atlanta as the site for the 2001 PGA Championship was announced at Winged Foot Golf Club, where this year's PGA begins on Thursday.
Jones, the last player to win all four of golf's most important championships in one year, learned the game at the Atlanta Athletic Club, where he maintained a membership throughout his life.
